questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following curve represents the first order reaction ?
options: (A) t_{1/2} vs [R]_0 (linear increasing graph starting from origin)
(B) t_{1/2} vs [R]_0 (horizontal straight line independent of [R]_0)
questions.solution: For a first order reaction, $t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k}$, which is independent of the initial concentration $[R]_0$. Therefore, a plot of $t_{1/2}$ versus $[R]_0$ is a horizontal straight line parallel to the concentration axis (Graph B).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following solutions will have the lowest freezing point in water ?
questions.solution: Depression in freezing point $\Delta T_f = i \cdot K_f \cdot m$. The compound that produces the maximum number of ions (highest van 't Hoff factor $i$) will show the maximum depression in freezing point, hence the lowest freezing point. $\text{CaCl}_2$ dissociates into 3 ions ($i = 3$), giving the maximum value of $i$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following is not a transition metal ?
questions.solution: Mercury (Hg) has fully filled d-orbitals in its ground state ($5d^{10}6s^2$) as well as in its common oxidation states, so it is not regarded as a transition metal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following represents the fraction of molecules with energies equal to or greater than $E_a$ ?
questions.solution: According to the Boltzmann distribution / Arrhenius equation, the fraction of molecules possessing kinetic energy equal to or greater than the activation energy $E_a$ is represented by the Boltzmann factor $e^{-E_a/RT}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What will happen during the electrolysis of aqueous solution of $\text{CuCl}_2$ by using platinum electrodes ?
options: H2 gas will be released at cathode
O2 gas will be released at anode
Cl2 gas will be released at anode
questions.solution: During electrolysis of aqueous $\text{CuCl}_2$, $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ions are reduced at the cathode to form copper metal, while $\text{Cl}^-$ ions are oxidized at the anode to release chlorine gas ($\text{Cl}_2$) due to overpotential considerations relative to oxygen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Aspirin is obtained by acetylation of
questions.solution: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) is produced by the acetylation of 2-hydroxybenzoic acid (salicylic acid) using acetic anhydride in the presence of an acid catalyst.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The secondary valency of $\text{Co}$ in the complex $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5(\text{NO}_2)]^{2+}$ is
questions.solution: Secondary valency corresponds to the coordination number of the central metal atom. Here, $\text{Co}$ is coordinated to five $\text{NH}_3$ ligands and one $\text{NO}_2^-$ ligand, making the coordination number equal to $5 + 1 = 6$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: At low temperature, phenol reacts with dil. $\text{HNO}_3$ to yield
questions.solution: Reaction of phenol with dilute $\text{HNO}_3$ at low temperature (298 K) yields a mixture of ortho-nitrophenol and para-nitrophenol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following is 'not' true about enantiomers ?
options: They have the same chemical reactivity.
They have the same specific rotation.
They have the same melting or boiling point.
They have the same refractive index.
questions.solution: Enantiomers have specific rotations equal in magnitude but opposite in sign (direction). Thus, saying they have the exact 'same specific rotation' is not true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Aniline on direct nitration yields
questions.solution: Direct nitration of aniline in strongly acidic medium leads to the formation of anilinium ion (meta-directing), resulting in 51% para, 47% meta, and 2% ortho derivatives.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following amines has lowest $pK_b$ value ?
questions.solution: Lower $pK_b$ value indicates stronger basic character. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{NH}(\text{CH}_3)$ (N-methylaniline) is more basic than aniline because the electron-donating methyl group increases the electron density on the nitrogen atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The deficiency of which of the following vitamins causes increased fragility of red blood cells and muscular weakness :
questions.solution: Deficiency of Vitamin E causes increased fragility of RBCs and muscular weakness.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A) : It is not possible to separate the components of an azeotrope by fractional distillation.
Reason (R) : Components of an azeotrope have the same composition in liquid and vapour phase and boil at a constant temperature.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Azeotropes boil at a constant temperature and have identical composition in liquid and vapour phases, so fractional distillation cannot separate their components. Both statements are true and R correctly explains A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A) : The presence of -OH group in phenols directs the incoming group to meta position in the ring.
Reason (R) : -OH group in phenols activates the aromatic ring towards electrophilic substitution reaction.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Assertion is false because the $-\text{OH}$ group in phenol is ortho- and para-directing (not meta). Reason is true because $-\text{OH}$ is strongly activating via resonance.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A) : Actinoids show wide range of oxidation states.
Reason (R) : Actinoids are radioactive in nature.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Actinoids show a wide range of oxidation states due to the comparable energies of $5f, 6d$ and $7s$ orbitals. They are also radioactive in nature. Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Assertion (A) : The pentaacetate of glucose does not react with $\text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{OH}$.
Reason (R) : It indicates the presence of free -CHO group in glucose.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution: Assertion is true because glucose pentaacetate does not form an oxime with hydroxylamine. Reason is false because this lack of reaction indicates the absence of a free $-\text{CHO}$ group in glucose pentaacetate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What type of deviation from Raoult’s law is shown by a mixture of phenol and aniline ? Give reason. What will happen to the boiling point of the solution on mixing phenol and aniline ?
questions.solution:
1. Phenol and aniline mixture shows **negative deviation** from Raoult's law.
2. **Reason:** The intermolecular hydrogen bonding between phenolic proton and nitrogen lone pair of aniline (Phenol-Aniline interaction) is stronger than solute-solute and solvent-solvent interactions.
3. **Boiling Point:** The boiling point of the solution will **increase** compared to the individual components (forms a maximum boiling azeotrope).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Why are haloarenes less reactive towards nucleophilic substitution reaction ? Give two reasons.
questions.solution:
Haloarenes are less reactive towards nucleophilic substitution due to:
1. **Resonance effect:** C-X bond develops partial double bond character, making bond cleavage difficult.
2. **Difference in hybridization of carbon:** The C-X bond carbon is $sp^2$ hybridized, which holds electrons more tightly than $sp^3$ carbon, shortening and strengthening the C-X bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(a) Write IUPAC names of the following coordination compounds :
(i) $[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2] [\text{Ag}(\text{CN})_2]$
(ii) $\text{K}_3[\text{Fe}(\text{C}_2\text{O}_4)_3]$

OR

(b) (i) Give a chemical test to show that $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{SO}_4]\text{Cl}$ and $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{SO}_4$ are ionisation isomers.
(ii) What is meant by the 'Chelate effect' ? Give an example.
questions.solution:
(a) (i) Diammineargentum(I) dicyanoargentate(I)
(ii) Potassium trioxalatoferrate(III)

OR

(b) (i) Add $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution: $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{SO}_4]\text{Cl}$ gives a white precipitate of $\text{AgCl}$, whereas $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{SO}_4$ gives no precipitate with $\text{AgNO}_3$. Add $\text{BaCl}_2$ solution: $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{SO}_4$ gives white precipitate of $\text{BaSO}_4$.
(ii) Chelate effect is the enhanced stability of complexes containing chelating (polydentate) ligands compared to similar complexes with monodentate ligands. Example: $[\text{Co}(\text{en})_3]^{3+}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Differentiate between the following :
(i) Peptide linkage and Glycosidic linkage
(ii) Essential amino acids and Non-essential amino acids
questions.solution:
(i) Peptide linkage is an amide linkage ($-\text{CO}-\text{NH}-$) formed between $-\text{COOH}$ and $-\text{NH}_2$ groups of amino acids in proteins. Glycosidic linkage is an oxide linkage ($-\text{O}-$) formed between two monosaccharide units by loss of water.
(ii) Essential amino acids cannot be synthesized in the body and must be obtained through diet (e.g., Valine, Leucine). Non-essential amino acids can be synthesized by the human body (e.g., Glycine, Alanine).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Following reaction takes place in one step :
$$2\text{A} + \text{B} \rightarrow 2\text{C}$$
How will the rate of above reaction change if the volume of the reaction vessel is decreased to one third of its original volume ? Will there be any change in the order of reaction with the reduced volume ?
questions.solution:
For an elementary one-step reaction, Rate $R_1 = k[A]^2[B]$.
When volume $V$ is decreased to $V/3$, the concentrations of $A$ and $B$ increase by 3 times: $[A'] = 3[A]$ and $[B'] = 3[B]$.
New Rate $R_2 = k(3[A])^2 (3[B]) = 27 \cdot k[A]^2[B] = 27 R_1$.
Thus, the rate increases by **27 times**.
There will be **no change** in the order of reaction (it remains third order).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
For the first order thermal decomposition reaction, following data was obtained :
$$\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}(g) \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_4(g) + \text{HCl}(g)$$
S. No. 1 | Time = 0 s | Total Pressure = 0.30 atm
S. No. 2 | Time = 30 s | Total Pressure = 0.50 atm
Calculate rate constant. [Given : $\log 3 = 0.48$]
questions.solution:
Let initial pressure of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$ be $P_i = 0.30\text{ atm}$.
At time $t=30\text{ s}$, let pressure decrease by $x\text{ atm}$.
$\text{Total pressure } P_t = (0.30 - x) + x + x = 0.30 + x = 0.50 \Rightarrow x = 0.20\text{ atm}$.
Pressure of reactant at $t=30\text{ s}$: $P_{\text{reactant}} = 0.30 - 0.20 = 0.10\text{ atm}$.
Rate constant $k = \frac{2.303}{t} \log\left(\frac{P_i}{P_{\text{reactant}}}\right) = \frac{2.303}{30} \log\left(\frac{0.30}{0.10}\right) = \frac{2.303}{30} \log 3 = \frac{2.303 \times 0.48}{30} \approx 0.0368\text{ s}^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(a) Answer the following :
(i) Why is the Equilibrium Constant ($K_c$) related to $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$ and not to $E_{\text{cell}}$ ?
(ii) Two metals 'A' and 'B' have standard electrode potential values of $-0.24\text{ V}$ and $+0.80\text{ V}$ respectively. Which of these will liberate hydrogen gas from dil. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ ?
(iii) Write the cell reaction which occurs in lead storage battery when it is in charging.

OR

(b) What type of battery is Mercury cell ? Why it is more advantageous than dry cell ? Write overall reaction taking place in Mercury cell.
questions.solution:
(a) (i) At equilibrium, $E_{\text{cell}} = 0$, so $\Delta G = 0$. $\Delta G^\circ = -RT \ln K_c = -nFE^\circ_{\text{cell}}$, relating $K_c$ specifically to $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$.
(ii) Metal 'A' ($-0.24\text{ V}$) has a negative standard reduction potential lower than $\text{H}^+/\text{H}_2$ ($0\text{ V}$), so it will liberate hydrogen gas.
(iii) Charging reaction: $2\text{PbSO}_4(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) \rightarrow \text{Pb}(s) + \text{PbO}_2(s) + 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4(aq)$.

OR

(b) Mercury cell is a primary battery. It is advantageous because its cell potential remains constant (approx 1.35 V) throughout its life as no gas or ions are involved whose concentrations change. Overall reaction: $\text{Zn(Hg)} + \text{HgO}(s) \rightarrow \text{ZnO}(s) + \text{Hg}(l)$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Calculate the boiling point of a solution containing $0.61\text{ g}$ of benzoic acid (Molar mass $= 122\text{ g mol}^{-1}$) in $5\text{ g}$ of $\text{CS}_2$ in which it dimerises to the extent of $88\%$. The boiling point and $K_b$ of $	ext{CS}_2$ are $46.2^\circ\text{C}$ and $2.3\text{ K kg mol}^{-1}$ respectively.
questions.solution:
Degree of association $\alpha = 0.88$, $n = 2$.
van 't Hoff factor $i = 1 - \alpha\left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right) = 1 - 0.88(0.5) = 1 - 0.44 = 0.56$.
Molality $m = \frac{w_b / M_b}{w_a / 1000} = \frac{0.61 / 122}{5 / 1000} = \frac{0.005}{0.005} = 1\text{ m}$.
$\Delta T_b = i \cdot K_b \cdot m = 0.56 \times 2.3 \times 1 = 1.288^\circ\text{C}$.
Boiling point of solution $= 46.2 + 1.288 = 47.488^\circ\text{C} \approx 47.5^\circ\text{C}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Write the reactions of D-Glucose with the following :
(a) $\text{HI}$
(b) $\text{Br}_2$ water
(c) Conc. $\text{HNO}_3$
questions.solution:
(a) D-Glucose $+ \text{HI} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{n-hexane} (\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3)$.
(b) D-Glucose $+ \text{Br}_2 \text{ water} \rightarrow \text{Gluconic acid} (\text{HOOC}-(\text{CHOH})_4-\text{CH}_2\text{OH})$.
(c) D-Glucose $+ \text{Conc. HNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{Saccharic acid} (\text{HOOC}-(\text{CHOH})_4-\text{COOH})$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Give reasons for the following :
(a) Carboxylic acids have higher boiling point than alcohols of comparable molecular masses.
(b) Alpha ($\alpha$) hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones are acidic in nature.
(c) Nucleophilic addition of ammonia and its derivatives does not occur with carbonyl group in strongly acidic medium.
questions.solution:
(a) Carboxylic acids form extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding resulting in stable dimers even in the vapour phase.
(b) The strong electron-withdrawing effect of the carbonyl group ($>C=O$) combined with resonance stabilization of the conjugate base (enolate ion) makes $\alpha$-hydrogens acidic.
(c) In strongly acidic medium, ammonia and its derivatives get protonated to form ammonium salts which are non-nucleophilic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Write the reaction involved in the following :
(a) Reimer-Tiemann reaction
(b) Kolbe's reaction
(c) Friedel-Crafts acylation of anisole
questions.solution:
(a) Phenol $+ \text{CHCl}_3 + 3\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde)} + 3\text{NaCl} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
(b) Phenol $+ \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Sodium phenoxide} \xrightarrow[2. \text{H}^+]{1. \text{CO}_2} \text{Salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid)}$.
(c) Anisole $+ \text{CH}_3\text{COCl} \xrightarrow{\text{Anhy. AlCl}_3} \text{2-methoxyacetophenone} + \text{4-methoxyacetophenone (major)}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Compound 'X' with molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Br}$ reacts with aqueous $\text{KOH}$ to give an alcohol. The rate of this reaction depends only on the concentration of the compound 'X'. When an optically active isomer 'Y' of the compound 'X' was treated with aqueous $\text{KOH}$ solution, the rate of reaction was found to be dependent on concentration of compound 'Y' and aqueous $\text{KOH}$ both.
(a) Write down the structural formula of both 'X' and 'Y'.
(b) Out of 'X' and 'Y', which one will undergo racemisation and why ?
(c) Out of 'X' and 'Y', which one will form product with inversion of configuration and why ?
questions.solution:
(a) 'X' undergoes $S_N1$ (rate depends only on [X]), so 'X' is 2-bromo-2-methylpropane (tert-butyl bromide, $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CBr}$). 'Y' undergoes $S_N2$ (rate depends on both [Y] and [KOH]) and is optically active, so 'Y' is 2-bromobutane ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH(Br)} \text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$).
(b) 'X' undergoes racemisation because it proceeds via planar carbocation intermediate formed in $S_N1$ mechanism.
(c) 'Y' forms product with inversion of configuration because it undergoes $S_N2$ reaction involving backside attack of nucleophile.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Read the passage and answer the questions:
(a) (i) Why $\text{CH}_3-\text{NH}_2$ is a stronger base than $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{N}$ in aqueous solution ?
(ii) Write structural formulae of the compound A and B :
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CONH}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{NaOBr}} \text{A} \xrightarrow[\text{Base}]{\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCl}} \text{B}$$
(b) A compound 'X' with molecular formula $\text{C}_3\text{H}_9\text{N}$ reacts with Hinsberg reagent to give a product insoluble in alkali. Identify 'X'.
OR
(b) How can you convert aniline to benzonitrile ?
(c) Why is $-\text{NH}_2$ group of aniline acetylated before carrying out nitration ?
questions.solution:
(a) (i) In aqueous solution, $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_3^+$ is stabilized by extensive hydration compared to $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{NH}^+$ due to steric hindrance to hydration in tertiary amine.
(ii) A = $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$ (methylamine, via Hoffmann bromamide reaction).
B = $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CONHCH}_3$ (N-methylbenzamide).
(b) 'X' is a secondary amine: $\text{CH}_3-\text{NH}-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$ (N-methylethanamine).
OR
(b) Aniline $\xrightarrow{\text{NaNO}_2 + \text{HCl}, 0-5^\circ\text{C}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- \xrightarrow{\text{CuCN/KCN}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CN}$ (benzonitrile).
(c) Acetylation reduces the activating power of $-\text{NH}_2$ group by resonance delocalization of lone pair into acetyl carbonyl, preventing over-nitration and meta-isomer formation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Answer the following based on CFT and VBT:
(a) In octahedral crystal field, energies of which d-orbitals will be raised when ligands approach the central metal atom/ion ? Give reason in support of your answer.
(b) Using crystal field theory, write the electronic configuration of central metal atom/ion of the following :
(i) $[\text{CoF}_6]^{3-}$
(ii) $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ [At. No. : Co = 27]
(c) $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$ is paramagnetic while $[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_4]$ is diamagnetic though both are tetrahedral. Why ? [Atomic No. : Ni = 28]
OR
(c) Write hybridization and magnetic behaviour of the complex $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}$. [Atomic No. : Fe = 26]
questions.solution:
(a) $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $d_{z^2}$ ($e_g$ set) orbitals experience greater repulsion because their lobes lie directly along the axes where ligands approach.
(b) $\text{Co}^{3+} (3d^6)$:
(i) $\text{F}^-$ is a weak field ligand ($\Delta_o < P$): configuration is $t_{2g}^4 e_g^2$.
(ii) $\text{NH}_3$ is a strong field ligand ($\Delta_o > P$): configuration is $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$.
(c) In $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$, $\text{Cl}^-$ is weak field, leading to $sp^3$ hybridization with 2 unpaired electrons ($3d^8$), hence paramagnetic. In $[\text{Ni}(\text{CO})_4]$, strong field $\text{CO}$ forces pairing of $4s^2$ electrons into $3d$, forming $3d^{10}$ and $sp^3$ with zero unpaired electrons, hence diamagnetic.
OR
(c) $[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}$ has $\text{Fe}^{3+} (3d^5)$. Strong ligand $\text{CN}^-$ causes pairing leaving 1 unpaired electron. Hybridization: $d^2sp^3$, Magnetic behavior: Paramagnetic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(a) (i) An organic compound (X) has the molecular formula $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$. Draw structures for (X) if it :
(I) does not give Tollen's test but gives a positive iodoform test.
(II) does not give Tollen's test and iodoform test but undergoes Aldol condensation.
(III) undergoes Cannizzaro's reaction.
(ii) Show how each of the following compounds can be converted to benzoic acid :
(I) Acetophenone
(II) Ethyl benzene

OR

(b) Answer the following questions :
(i) Draw structure of the 2, 4-dinitrophenyl hydrazone derivative of benzaldehyde.
(ii) Arrange the following in increasing order of their reactivity towards HCN :
Di-tert. butyl ketone, Acetaldehyde, Acetone
(iii) Give a simple chemical test to distinguish between benzoic acid and ethyl benzoate.
(iv) Write the name of the reagent to convert Ethanenitrile to Ethanal.
(v) Draw the structure of 'X' in the reaction: Cyclohexanol + $\text{CrO}_3 \rightarrow \text{X}$.
questions.solution:
(a) (i) (I) Pentan-2-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$)
(II) Pentan-3-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$)
(III) 2,2-Dimethylpropanal ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCHO}$)
(ii) (I) Acetophenone $+ \text{I}_2/\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COONa} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$
(II) Ethyl benzene $+ \text{KMnO}_4/\text{KOH}, \Delta \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOK} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}$

OR

(b) (i) $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{CH}=\text{N}-\text{NH}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_3(\text{NO}_2)_2$
(ii) Di-tert. butyl ketone < Acetone < Acetaldehyde
(iii) Benzoic acid gives brisk effervescence with $\text{NaHCO}_3$ solution releasing $\text{CO}_2$ gas, whereas ethyl benzoate does not.
(iv) DIBAL-H followed by $H_3O^+$ (or $\text{SnCl}_2/\text{HCl}$ - Stephen reduction).
(v) Cyclohexanone.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(a) (i) From the given data of $E^\circ_{\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M}}$ values (V: -1.18, Cr: -0.91, Mn: -1.18, Fe: -0.44, Co: -0.28, Ni: -0.25, Cu: +0.34 V):
(I) Why $E^\circ_{\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M}}$ show irregular trend in the above values ?
(II) Why is $E^\circ_{\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}}$ value exceptionally positive ?
(III) Why $E^\circ_{\text{Mn}^{2+}/\text{Mn}}$ value is highly negative ?
(ii) Write the ionic equations for the oxidising action of potassium permanganate for its reaction with $\text{I}^-$ in both acidic and alkaline solutions.

OR

(b) (i) Name a member of the lanthanoid series which exhibits +4 and +2 oxidation states.
(ii) Why transition metals act as good catalyst ?
(iii) Why Cr has higher melting point than Mn ?
(iv) What happens when acidic solution of potassium permanganate is allowed to stand for sometime ? Give the equation involved.
questions.solution:
(a) (i) (I) Due to irregular variation in ionization enthalpies ($\Delta_i H_1 + \Delta_i H_2$) and sublimation enthalpies.
(II) High enthalpy of atomization and low hydration enthalpy of $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ fail to compensate for high ionization enthalpy.
(III) Stable half-filled $3d^5$ configuration of $\text{Mn}^{2+}$.
(ii) Acidic: $2\text{MnO}_4^- + 10\text{I}^- + 16\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 5\text{I}_2 + 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
Alkaline: $2\text{MnO}_4^- + \text{I}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{MnO}_2 + \text{IO}_3^- + 2\text{OH}^-$.

OR

(b) (i) +4: Cerium (Ce); +2: Europium (Eu).
(ii) Ability to show variable oxidation states and provide large surface area for adsorption.
(iii) $\text{Cr}$ ($3d^5 4s^1$) has 6 unpaired electrons available for metallic bonding, whereas $\text{Mn}$ has a stable $3d^5$ half-filled subshell resulting in weaker metallic bonding.
(iv) It decomposes slowly releasing oxygen gas: $4\text{MnO}_4^- + 4\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 4\text{MnO}_2 + 3\text{O}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (Auto-reduction).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
(a) Calculate emf and $\Delta G$ for the following cell at 298 K :
$$\text{Mg}(s) / \text{Mg}^{2+}(0.01\text{ M}) // \text{Ag}^+(0.001\text{ M}) / \text{Ag}(s)$$
Given : $E^\circ_{\text{Mg}^{2+}/\text{Mg}} = -2.37\text{ V}, E^\circ_{\text{Ag}^+/\text{Ag}} = +0.80\text{ V}$
[$1\text{ F} = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}, \log 10 = 1$]
